title.narrative: Kvinna till kvinna GBV and women economic empowerment Serbia 2022-2026
Kvinna till kvinna GBV och kvinnors ekonomiska egenmakt Serbien 2022-2026

description.narrative: Kvinna till kvinna and partner organisations influence improvements in policy and practice regarding GBV and women's economic empowerment.
Kvinna till kvinna och samarbetsorganisationer påverkar förbättringar i policy och praxis när det gäller GBV och kvinnors ekonomiska egenmakt.

The objectives of the contribution are:
Overall Programme objective: Kvinna till Kvinna and partner organisations influence improvements in policy and practice regarding gender-based violence and womens economic empowerment in Serbia.
Specific objective 1 - Partner organisations and other relevant actors reached within the Project contribute to changes in attitude, practice and policy regarding GBV, based on the Istanbul Convention
Specific objective 2 - Organisations reached within the Project contribute to changes in policy and practice regarding womens economic empowerment.
Specific objective 3 - Increased sustainability and visibility of partner organisations and other relevant actors within the Project, and for their results

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls
Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
Example of results:
The SOS hotline run by Autonomous Womens Centre (AWC) rang 3,686 calls from 1,116 women (916 new). Thanks to flexible core funding, AWC could provide individual ("face to face") consultations, of which there were 704 conversations with 201 women (78 new). This is an increase of 17.7% compared to the previous year. Two hundred and twenty-one e-mail (written) consultations were carried out with the provision of emotional support, information and referral to other services for 131 women. Of the 4,611 services provided, 2,568 (70%) were related to psychosocial support and 1,118 (30%) to informational interviews. Legal aid services were provided to 684 victims/survivors of violence (466 new). In 2024, 1,652 services were provided, of which 1,534 were oral legal assistance (870 by telephone, 260 by email, 35 directly in the AWC premises, 367 via Viber/WhatsApp/signal) and 118 written legal assistance. Five workshops were held in Belgrade, Batoina, and Mirijevo and a total of 91 young people (75 girls and 16 boys) between the ages of 14 and 30 improved their knowledge about different forms of violence and the impact pornography has on violence in intimate partner relationships. Yet again, the work of AWC during this reporting period, just as in other reporting periods, showed that they are among the main actors implementing the Istanbul Convention since the Serbian institutions are overall failing in this regard.
In synergy with the regional, Sida-funded EU-advocacy programme, AWC had the opportunity to again join the advocacy week in Brussels in November 2024, and bring forward key information and recommendations regarding GBV in Serbia, based on data from WCSOs in the country, as well as updates on Serbias failure to implement Istanbul Convention requirements, and challenges they faced as members of the working group for amendments to the Criminal Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure regarding acts of GBV.
Victimology Sociey of Serbia held two trainings for working with victims/survivors of violence. The first training was delivered for 13 women activists from CSOs within the Women Against Violence Network. The second training was organised for a group of 24 women participants from social welfare services, schools and pre-school institutions (psychologists and pedagogues).
Impuls from Tutin, as the only autonomous women's and feminist organisation in that part of Serbia, continued to cooperate with institutions from Tutin and Novi Pazar, involved in the fight against GBV.
Twenty representatives of institutions were trained in operating in the field of protection against violence (health, schools, police, public prosecutor's office, centre for social work) from the municipalities of Novi Pazar and Tutin). Activist of Impuls, Tutin implemented 128 services for women in situation of violence.
